title: The Montgolfier Brothers Send Up a Balloon
text:
Joseph-Michel and Jacques-Etienne Montgolfier were two of the sixteen children of a paper manufacturer in Annonay, in southern France. Joseph, the elder, was a restless inventor and dreamer with little head for business. Etienne, five years younger, had trained as an architect and was called home to run the family paper mill, which he did with skill.

In 1782 Joseph became convinced that a light bag filled with heated air could rise. He tested the idea with small envelopes of silk and paper, and brought his brother into the work. The two built ever larger balloons from cloth lined with paper, the product of their own mill. On 4 June 1783 they launched an unmanned balloon in the market square of Annonay before a crowd. It rose to a great height and came down more than a mile away.

The news reached Paris, and Etienne, the more polished of the two, went there to repeat the demonstration. On 19 September 1783, at Versailles, before King Louis XVI and Marie Antoinette, a balloon lifted a sheep, a duck and a rooster, which landed safely. On 21 November 1783, a Montgolfier balloon carried two men, Jean-Francois Pilatre de Rozier and the Marquis d'Arlandes, over Paris in the first free flight of human beings. The king ennobled the brothers' father in recognition.
lesson: Partners with different gifts can achieve together what neither could alone. A dreamer needs an organizer, and an organizer needs a dream.
source: Charles Coulston Gillispie, The Montgolfier Brothers and the Invention of Aviation (1983)
